  ## Code review findings — story 6.2 diff
  
  - **`lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart:143-145`** — `_cachedSessions()`'s sort still uses `DateTime.parse(...).compareTo(...)` (throws on malformed input), even though this exact review round fixed the two sibling "most recent session" sorts (`ChatCubit._bootstrap` and the new `_ConversasSection` in `app_drawer.dart`) to use `DateTime.tryParse(...) ?? DateTime(0)` for crash safety. The diff's own `deferred-work.md` entry explicitly names all three sites as duplicates of the same comparator, but only two got the fix. A cached session whose JSON decodes fine but whose `updatedAt` isn't valid ISO-8601 will throw an uncaught `FormatException` out of `listSessions()`'s offline/timeout fallback path instead of returning `Left(Failure)`, violating RNF09 ("no repository signature outside this pattern"). Verified by reading the live file (not just the diff hunk): the per-item `try/catch` only wraps decoding, not the sort that runs after the loop, and `listSessions()` calls `_cachedSessions()` with no surrounding try/catch either.
  
  - **`lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:407-419` (`_cancelInFlightSend`)** — it resets the internal `_isSending` flag but never emits an updated `ChatReady`. In both `switchSession` and `startNewSession`, this is called *before* the subsequent `listMessages`/`createSession` call; if that call then fails (`Left`), the method returns the `Left` without emitting anything, leaving the still-current `ChatReady.isSending` stuck at `true` forever — nothing else will flip it back. Since `_ChatComposer`'s `canSend = state is ChatReady && !state.isSending` (chat_screen.dart:304), the composer becomes permanently disabled for a session the user never actually left, even though the underlying send was genuinely cancelled. None of the new "cross-session stream leakage" tests cover the combination of "an in-flight send is cancelled" + "the switch/create call itself then fails" — the existing tests only exercise the success path of that combination.
  
  - **`lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart` (`_send`)** — `_textController.clear()` only happens on send; nothing clears (or preserves per-session) the composer's draft text when `switchSession`/`startNewSession` fires. A partially typed, unsent message silently carries over verbatim into whatever different session becomes active, with no AC, Design Note, or test addressing it.
  
  - **`lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart` (`_ConversasSection.build`)** — the `for (final session in sorted) _DrawerSessionItem(...)` loop gives each row no `key`. When the list reorders (a new session prepended by `startNewSession`, or relative ordering shifting), Flutter has no stable widget identity to diff against, risking state/ripple-animation continuity bugs across rebuilds.
  
  - **`lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart` (`_jumpToOffset`)** — its `addPostFrameCallback` only checks `_scrollController.hasClients`, never `mounted`, unlike the near-identical `_focusComposerSoon` right beside it which does check `mounted`. This inconsistency leaves `_jumpToOffset` unguarded against a dispose race if the screen unmounts between the session switch and the next frame.
  
  - **`lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart`** — the new `BlocBuilder<ChatCubit, ChatState>` wrapping `_ConversasSection` has no `buildWhen`, so it rebuilds (re-sorts every session, rebuilds every `_DrawerSessionItem`) on *every* `ChatReady` emission — including once per streamed AI token — even while the drawer is closed and off-screen, since `Scaffold.drawer` stays mounted in the widget tree regardless of visibility. This is a new, previously-undisclosed rebuild-churn source distinct from the already-deferred `ChatScreen._scrollToBottomSoon` one.
  
  - **Status tracking mismatch** — the new `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-6-2-multi-session-chat-history-new-conversation.md` frontmatter declares `status: 'done'`, while `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/sprint-status.yaml` marks the same story `6-2-...: review`. The two trackers disagree about whether the story is actually finished.
  
  - **`lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart` (`_recordScrollOffset`)** — the scroll listener has no awareness of an in-progress session transition. During the frame that rebuilds the `ListView` for a newly switched-to session (before `_jumpToOffset`'s post-frame callback runs), Flutter's automatic scroll-position clamp can fire this listener and record a transient, incorrect offset under the *new* session's id. It's self-corrected moments later once `_jumpToOffset` runs, but it's an untested latent fragility, and the guard that already exists for this exact class of problem (`_lastSessionId`) isn't reused here.
  
  - **Accessibility gap not previously flagged** — switching the entire active conversation (`switchSession`/`startNewSession`) replaces the whole message list with no `Semantics` announcement or focus-traversal reset communicating "the conversation changed" to a screen-reader user; this is distinct from the already-deferred "active row color-only cue" and "no live region for streaming text" findings — here the gap is about the navigation action itself, not the drawer row or the streaming bubble.
  
  - **Process/traceability gap** — `test/features/chat/chat_flow_e2e_test.dart` and its `test-summary.md` write-up are explicitly scoped to closing a **story 6.1** coverage gap ("chat's first vertical slice had no `*_flow_e2e_test.dart` at all"), yet this work is bundled inside story 6.2's diff/commit with no cross-reference in `sprint-status.yaml` or the 6-2 spec's own Verification section noting that this e2e suite proves 6-1's acceptance, not 6-2's. Anyone auditing "what proves 6.2 is done" later has to know to look for a file whose own header says it's about 6.1.
  
  - **`lib/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart` (`sendMessage`'s buffer fix)** — `buffer = (buffer + chunk).replaceAll('\r\n', '\n')` re-scans and reallocates the *entire* accumulated buffer on every incoming chunk (not just the newly appended portion), rather than normalizing only the tail that could contain a split `\r\n`. Functionally correct, but it reintroduces O(n) work per chunk over whatever of the buffer hasn't yet been flushed by the `\n\n` splitter, with no test or comment acknowledging the trade-off was deliberate.
  
  Methodology note: I read the full 2365-line diff file in four sequential passes (offsets 0, 600, 1200, 1800) before forming this review, and cross-checked the two most consequential findings (the `DateTime.parse` crash risk and the `_cancelInFlightSend`/`isSending` stuck-state bug) against the live files in the repo (`lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart`, `lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart`, `lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart`) to confirm they reflect the current working tree, not just the diff hunks in isolation.
</agent-message>

# Step 3: Triage

## RULES

- YOU MUST ALWAYS SPEAK OUTPUT in your Agent communication style with the config `{communication_language}`

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. **Normalize** findings from all layers into a unified list where each finding has:
   - `id` -- sequential integer
   - `source` -- the `id` of the layer that produced the finding (e.g., `blind-hunter`), or merged sources joined with `+` (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`)
   - `title` -- one-line summary
   - `detail` -- full description
   - `location` -- file and line reference (if available)

2. **Deduplicate.** Deduplicate only findings with the same claim and same required action. If two or more findings meet both conditions, merge them into one:
   - Use the most specific finding as the base (prefer findings with a precise location over prose-only findings).
   - Append any unique detail, reasoning, or location references from the other finding(s) into the surviving `detail` field.
   - Set `source` to the merged sources (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`).

3. Then evaluate each remaining finding independently. Do not reject a finding because a related finding was rejected.

4. **Read the code before rating.** Before assigning severity, open the source at each finding's location and read enough surrounding code to judge reachability -- call sites, guards, and validation that live outside the diff hunk. Do not rate from the diff hunk alone. Severity reflects the real consequence at a real call site, not the worst theoretical reading.

5. **Assign severity** to each finding by consequence for the artifact's main consumer (software user, document reader, etc).
   Disregard any severity assigned by a reviewing subagent. Review subagents operate under by-design information asymmetry and do not have enough context to set final severity for this workflow.
   - `low` -- none or cosmetic
   - `medium` -- tolerable
   - `high` -- intolerable

6. **Route** each finding into exactly one triage bucket:
   - **decision_needed** -- There is an ambiguous choice that requires human input. The code cannot be correctly patched without knowing the user's intent. Only possible if `{review_mode}` = `"full"`.
   - **patch** -- Code issue that is fixable without human input. The correct fix is unambiguous.
   - **defer** -- Pre-existing issue not caused by the current change. Real but not actionable now.
   - **dismiss** -- Noise, false positive, or handled elsewhere.

   If `{review_mode}` = `"no-spec"` and a finding would otherwise be `decision_needed`, reclassify it as `patch` (if the fix is unambiguous) or `defer` (if not).

7. **Drop** all `dismiss` findings. Record the dismiss count for the summary.

8. If `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, report which layers failed before announcing results. If zero findings remain after dropping dismissed AND `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, warn the user that the review may be incomplete rather than announcing a clean review.

9. If zero findings remain after triage (all rejected or none raised): state "✅ Clean review — all layers passed." (Step 3 already warned if any review layers failed via `{failed_layers}`.)

## NEXT

Read fully and follow `./step-04-present.md`

### Review Findings (code review, round 2 — bmad-code-review, 2026-11-05)

Four parallel layers (blind-hunter, edge-case-hunter, verification-gap, acceptance-auditor) against the full baseline→HEAD diff, independent of the self-review above.

**Patch:**
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `ChatRepositoryImpl._cachedSessions()`'s offline-cache sort uses `DateTime.parse` (throws `FormatException`) on `updatedAt`, not `tryParse` — unlike the two sibling "most recent session" sorts in this same diff (`ChatCubit._bootstrap`, `_ConversasSection`), which both deliberately use `DateTime.tryParse(...) ?? DateTime(0)` for exactly this crash-safety reason. A cached session that decodes fine but carries a non-ISO-8601 `updatedAt` makes `listSessions()`'s offline/timeout fallback throw uncaught instead of resolving to `Left`, violating RNF09 and leaving `ChatCubit._bootstrap()` stuck in `ChatBootstrapLoading` with no test covering this path. Independently found by 4/4 review layers. [lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart:143-145]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `switchSession()`/`startNewSession()` leave `ChatReady.isSending` stuck at `true` when the post-cancel call fails. `_cancelInFlightSend()` resets the internal `_isSending` guard but never emits an updated state; if the subsequent `listMessages()`/`createSession()` call then returns `Left`, the method returns early with no `emit` at all. The still-current session's `ChatReady.isSending` (set `true` by the send `_cancelInFlightSend` just cancelled) is never flipped back — `_ChatComposer`'s `canSend = state is ChatReady && !state.isSending` (chat_screen.dart:304) leaves the composer permanently disabled for the rest of the app run, with no path back to `false` except restart. No test exercises "an in-flight send is cancelled" + "the switch/create call itself then fails" together. [lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:155-186, 196-223, 407-419]
- [ ] [Review][Patch] `ChatRemoteDataSource.listSessions()`/`listMessages()`'s per-item parse-isolation loop skips each malformed item but never checks whether *every* item in a non-empty response was skipped — it then returns `right(<empty list>)` indistinguishable from a legitimately empty response, instead of `left(Failure.malformedResponse(...))`. For `listSessions()` this would make `ChatCubit._bootstrap()` believe no session exists and spuriously `createSession()`, hiding the user's real sessions behind a new empty one; for `listMessages()` a session's whole history would silently render empty. [lib/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart:24-49 (listSessions), 66-92 (listMessages)]

**Defer:**
- [x] [Review][Defer] Unsent composer draft text carries over verbatim into whatever session becomes active after `switchSession`/`startNewSession` — `_textController` is only cleared on send, never on a session change. No acceptance criterion or Design Note covers draft handling across switches. [lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart] — deferred, pre-existing
- [x] [Review][Defer] The drawer's "CONVERSAS" `BlocBuilder<ChatCubit, ChatState>` has no `buildWhen`, so it re-sorts and rebuilds every session row on *every* `ChatReady` emission — including once per streamed AI token — even while the drawer is closed and off-screen (`Scaffold.drawer` stays mounted). Harmless today given small session counts; same unthrottled-rebuild class already deferred for `ChatScreen._scrollToBottomSoon` from story 6.1. [lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart] — deferred, pre-existing
- [x] [Review][Defer] Switching the active conversation (`switchSession`/`startNewSession`) replaces the whole message list with no `Semantics` announcement or focus-traversal reset communicating "the conversation changed" to a screen-reader user. No accessibility requirement is scoped for this story; matches the existing deferred a11y-debt pattern elsewhere in the codebase. [lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart, lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart] — deferred, pre-existing
- [x] [Review][Defer] `ChatRemoteDataSource.sendMessage()`'s `\r\n`-split-across-chunks fix (`buffer = (buffer + chunk).replaceAll('\r\n', '\n')`) re-scans and reallocates the *entire* accumulated buffer on every incoming chunk rather than normalizing only the newly appended tail. Functionally correct; negligible real cost given per-chunk buffer sizes, no test or comment acknowledges the trade-off. [lib/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart] — deferred, pre-existing
- [x] [Review][Defer] `_jumpToOffset`'s `addPostFrameCallback` checks `_scrollController.hasClients` but not `mounted`, unlike `_focusComposerSoon` right beside it which does. Mirrors the same unguarded pattern already present in the pre-existing sibling `_scrollToBottomSoon` since story 6.1 — not a new regression class introduced here. [lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart] — deferred, pre-existing
- [x] [Review][Defer] `ChatScreen._recordScrollOffset`'s scroll listener has no awareness of an in-progress session transition — during the frame that rebuilds the list for a newly switched-to session (before `_jumpToOffset`'s post-frame callback runs), an automatic scroll-position clamp can fire this listener and record a transient, incorrect offset under the *new* session's id. Self-corrects moments later once `_jumpToOffset` runs; untested latent fragility, no observed visual glitch. [lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart] — deferred, pre-existing

**Dismissed as noise (7):** `_DrawerSessionItem` rows missing a `Key` (cosmetic, no state/animation continuity need in a plain `Column` of stateless rows); the very first bootstrap `ChatReady` being treated as a "new session" by `_lastSessionId`'s null-initial value (working as designed — the code's own doc comment explicitly scopes this to "the initial bootstrap" as one of the triggering events, not an oversight); `switchSession(sessionId)` lacking validation that `sessionId` exists in `current.sessions` (unreachable — the only call site, `_ConversasSection.onSelect`, always passes an id sourced from that same session list); a theoretical concurrent-invocation race on `switchSession`/`startNewSession` (unreachable — `AppDrawer`'s own `_actionTaken` guard plus the drawer staying open throughout the `await` prevent a second call on the same instance, and `Navigator.pop()` only runs after the awaited result resolves); "Novo Chat" tapped during `ChatBootstrapLoading` giving no feedback (already self-disclosed as a known timing-window gap in this story's own `deferred-work.md` entry); a perceived mismatch between this spec's frontmatter `status: 'done'` and `sprint-status.yaml`'s `review` (not a bug — matches `sprint-status.yaml`'s own documented convention: spec status reflects the implementer's own build+self-review completion, external tracking only moves to `done` after this code-review gate, same pattern already used by spec-6-1); the bundled `chat_flow_e2e_test.dart`/`test-summary.md` work being scoped to story 6.1 rather than 6.2 (already self-disclosed — both the commit message and the test-summary's own header name story 6.1 explicitly).

+- [ ] [Review][Patch] `switchSession()`/`startNewSession()` leave `ChatReady.isSending` stuck at `true` when the post-cancel call fails. `_cancelInFlightSend()` resets the internal `_isSending` guard but never emits an updated state; if the subsequent `listMessages()`/`createSession()` call then returns `Left`, the method returns early with no `emit` at all. The still-current session's `ChatReady.isSending` (set `true` by the send `_cancelInFlightSend` just cancelled) is never flipped back — `_ChatComposer`'s `canSend = state is ChatReady && !state.isSending` (chat_screen.dart:304) leaves the composer permanently disabled for the rest of the app run, with no path back to `false` except restart. No test exercises "an in-flight send is cancelled" + "the switch/create call itself then fails" together. [lib/features/chat/presentation/cubit/chat_cubit.dart:155-186, 196-223, 407-419]

+- [ ] [Review][Patch] `ChatRemoteDataSource.listSessions()`/`listMessages()`'s per-item parse-isolation loop skips each malformed item but never checks whether *every* item in a non-empty response was skipped — it then returns `right(<empty list>)` indistinguishable from a legitimately empty response, instead of `left(Failure.malformedResponse(...))`. For `listSessions()` this would make `ChatCubit._bootstrap()` believe no session exists and spuriously `createSession()`, hiding the user's real sessions behind a new empty one; for `listMessages()` a session's whole history would silently render empty. [lib/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart:24-49 (listSessions), 66-92 (listMessages)]

+- [x] [Review][Defer] Unsent composer draft text carries over verbatim into whatever session becomes active after `switchSession`/`startNewSession` — `_textController` is only cleared on send, never on a session change. No acceptance criterion or Design Note covers draft handling across switches. [lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart] — deferred, pre-existing

+- [x] [Review][Defer] The drawer's "CONVERSAS" `BlocBuilder<ChatCubit, ChatState>` has no `buildWhen`, so it re-sorts and rebuilds every session row on *every* `ChatReady` emission — including once per streamed AI token — even while the drawer is closed and off-screen (`Scaffold.drawer` stays mounted). Harmless today given small session counts; same unthrottled-rebuild class already deferred for `ChatScreen._scrollToBottomSoon` from story 6.1. [lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart] — deferred, pre-existing

+- [x] [Review][Defer] Switching the active conversation (`switchSession`/`startNewSession`) replaces the whole message list with no `Semantics` announcement or focus-traversal reset communicating "the conversation changed" to a screen-reader user. No accessibility requirement is scoped for this story; matches the existing deferred a11y-debt pattern elsewhere in the codebase. [lib/core/widgets/app_drawer.dart, lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart] — deferred, pre-existing

+- [x] [Review][Defer] `ChatRemoteDataSource.sendMessage()`'s `
`-split-across-chunks fix (`buffer = (buffer + chunk).replaceAll('
', '
')`) re-scans and reallocates the *entire* accumulated buffer on every incoming chunk rather than normalizing only the newly appended tail. Functionally correct; negligible real cost given per-chunk buffer sizes, no test or comment acknowledges the trade-off. [lib/features/chat/data/datasources/chat_remote_data_source.dart] — deferred, pre-existing

+- [x] [Review][Defer] `_jumpToOffset`'s `addPostFrameCallback` checks `_scrollController.hasClients` but not `mounted`, unlike `_focusComposerSoon` right beside it which does. Mirrors the same unguarded pattern already present in the pre-existing sibling `_scrollToBottomSoon` since story 6.1 — not a new regression class introduced here. [lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart] — deferred, pre-existing

+- [x] [Review][Defer] `ChatScreen._recordScrollOffset`'s scroll listener has no awareness of an in-progress session transition — during the frame that rebuilds the list for a newly switched-to session (before `_jumpToOffset`'s post-frame callback runs), an automatic scroll-position clamp can fire this listener and record a transient, incorrect offset under the *new* session's id. Self-corrects moments later once `_jumpToOffset` runs; untested latent fragility, no observed visual glitch. [lib/features/chat/presentation/screens/chat_screen.dart] — deferred, pre-existing

+**Dismissed as noise (7):** `_DrawerSessionItem` rows missing a `Key` (cosmetic, no state/animation continuity need in a plain `Column` of stateless rows); the very first bootstrap `ChatReady` being treated as a "new session" by `_lastSessionId`'s null-initial value (working as designed — the code's own doc comment explicitly scopes this to "the initial bootstrap" as one of the triggering events, not an oversight); `switchSession(sessionId)` lacking validation that `sessionId` exists in `current.sessions` (unreachable — the only call site, `_ConversasSection.onSelect`, always passes an id sourced from that same session list); a theoretical concurrent-invocation race on `switchSession`/`startNewSession` (unreachable — `AppDrawer`'s own `_actionTaken` guard plus the drawer staying open throughout the `await` prevent a second call on the same instance, and `Navigator.pop()` only runs after the awaited result resolves); "Novo Chat" tapped during `ChatBootstrapLoading` giving no feedback (already self-disclosed as a known timing-window gap in this story's own `deferred-work.md` entry); a perceived mismatch between this spec's frontmatter `status: 'done'` and `sprint-status.yaml`'s `review` (not a bug — matches `sprint-status.yaml`'s own documented convention: spec status reflects the implementer's own build+self-review completion, external tracking only moves to `done` after this code-review gate, same pattern already used by spec-6-1); the bundled `chat_flow_e2e_test.dart`/`test-summary.md` work being scoped to story 6.1 rather than 6.2 (already self-disclosed — both the commit message and the test-summary's own header name story 6.1 explicitly).
